# CodexMeter 1.3.0
CodexMeter 1.3.0 adds optional Claude Code support next to Codex: local token totals, private on-device analytics, and read-only five-hour and weekly limits, each kept fully separate from Codex data.
## What changed
- **Codex / Claude Code selector:** a logo-first switch at the top of the menu. Menu bar totals, Today, history, Usage / Projects / Sessions, and the Settings data actions all follow the selected service. - **Claude Code local usage:** Today, This Week, This Month, and Local History totals for this Mac, with model, project, and session drill-downs and sub-agent relationships. Read from `~/.claude/projects` (or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects` when set in the app's environment). - **Honest Claude accounting:** cache-read and cache-creation tokens are included in Input; repeated streaming blocks and copied history are deduplicated by response ID rather than summed. - **Read-only Claude limits:** the documented status-line five-hour and weekly percentages and reset times, shown after Claude Code completes a response. Any existing status-line command is preserved and restored on disconnect. - **Separate storage:** Claude usage lives in its own `Claude.sqlite`; the Codex database, schema, and counting rules are unchanged. - **Menu header parity:** the connected account now shows for both services in the same row (Claude shows its plan instead of a switcher).
## Setting up Claude Code
1. Open **Settings → Services** and enable **Claude Code**. 2. If you are already signed in to the `claude` CLI, choose **Add Account**. Otherwise run `claude` in your terminal and sign in there first, then choose **Add Account**. 3. The Claude tab appears in the menu only after this explicit setup. Use Claude Code once and press **Refresh** to populate limits.
CodexMeter runs only the read-only `claude auth status` command to identify the signed-in account. It never launches a login flow and never reads or copies Claude credentials. Disconnecting removes the status-line helper; it does not sign you out of Claude Code.
## Verification and limitations
- Automated tests cover Claude cache arithmetic, duplicate blocks, copied history, streaming revisions, restarts, local day/week/month boundaries, analytics reconciliation, sub-agents, history cutoffs, source isolation, status-line install and restore, account identity, and native layout in both appearances. Full suite: 276 tests, 0 failures (5 environment-integration tests skipped). - On real local logs, response-ID deduplication avoids roughly a 1.8× over-count versus naive summing. - The package is Universal 2 for Apple silicon and Intel Macs running macOS 14 or later. The bundled Claude limits helper is signed and verified as part of the release. - **Not included:** Claude web/mobile account-wide totals, Claude account switching, attachment counts, and API-equivalent cost estimates. Claude prices are not published here, so cost is never shown for Claude rather than displayed as an unavailable estimate. - Codex-only users are unaffected: Claude is off by default, its tab stays hidden, and the Codex database is untouched. - The app remains ad-hoc signed, without Apple Developer ID signing or notarization. SHA-256 protects the first download; Sparkle authenticates later update feeds and archives with Ed25519 signatures.
## Install or update with Homebrew
```bash brew update brew upgrade --cask --greedy HechoLP/tap/codexmeter ```
For a new installation:
```bash brew install --cask HechoLP/tap/codexmeter ```
Homebrew verifies the published ZIP checksum. If macOS blocks this certificate-free app after installation, confirm that it came from `HechoLP/tap/codexmeter`, then remove quarantine from this app only:
```bash xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/CodexMeter.app open /Applications/CodexMeter.app ```
## First direct-download launch
Download `CodexMeter-1.3.0.dmg` and `SHA256SUMS.txt` from this release into the same folder. Verify the checksum before opening the disk image:
```bash cd ~/Downloads grep ' CodexMeter-1.3.0.dmg$' SHA256SUMS.txt | shasum -a 256 -c - open CodexMeter-1.3.0.dmg ```
Only after the checksum reports `OK`, copy `CodexMeter.app` to Applications and use the app-scoped quarantine command above. Do not run an unverified download or disable Gatekeeper globally.
## Recovery
This release does not migrate the Codex usage database. Claude usage is stored separately and is only read when Claude Code is enabled and connected; earlier versions ignore it. Do not delete the local usage databases or saved Keychain entries when troubleshooting. Published version tags are immutable; corrections ship as a new patch release.
